slavery.name: Slavery
classes: There was slavery in at least a part
entries: The oldest known code of laws, written about 2100 to 2050 BCE in Sumer, has laws about slaves. The Code of Hammurabi of Babylon, of about 1750 BCE, also tells the free from the enslaved.

There was slavery in ancient Egypt at least from the Old Kingdom. The first record is from the reign of King Sneferu, in the 26th century BCE, about captives from wars in Nubia. The article follows slavery to the Ptolemaic Kingdom and to Roman Egypt.
Slavery was a widely accepted practice in ancient Greece. Most slaves worked on farms; others worked in quarries, in mines and in homes. The records are in pieces, and most of them are about Athens.

Slavery had an important part in the society and the economy of ancient Rome. By Roman law, slaves were property. Rome's oldest code of laws, of about 450 BCE, takes slavery as a given. In the years 260 to 425 CE, 10 to 15% of the people of the empire were slaves.
Slavery had a notable part in the economy of the Byzantine Empire. Many slaves came from wars. With time, laws gave slaves more rights, and slavery lost a part of its weight in the economy.
China under the Qin and Han dynasties

Under the Qin dynasty, men with a certain cruel punishment became slaves of the state and did forced work. The first Han emperor set free the farm workers who had been made slaves, but servants in homes stayed slaves.
Among the Maya, raids on the lands around them brought in victims for sacrifice and slaves who built temples. A child of a slave was usually born free.
In the 9th century, slaves of the Red Sea slave trade were taken to Jeddah, Mecca and Medina, and then by caravan across the desert to Baghdad, in the Abbasid Caliphate.
Enslaved Africans were taken across the Red Sea to Arabia and Yemen at least from the 1st century on. This trade is one of the longest in the world: it went on until the 1960s.
Sweden ended slavery in 1335, also in its lands in Finland. But on the Swedish island Saint Barthélemy in the Caribbean there was slavery from 1784 to 1847.
Sweden ended slavery in 1335, also in its lands in Finland. Finland was a part of Sweden then.

There was slavery in Poland in the Middle Ages. The source says that the Statutes of Casimir the Great freed the non-free people in 1347. Late in the 14th century serfdom, a different form of unfree work, took the place of slavery.
The Third Statute of Lithuania ended slavery in 1588. Serfdom, a different form of unfree work, went on until 1861.
Enslaved Africans were taken across the Red Sea to Arabia and Yemen at least from the 1st century on. Slavery in Yemen was banned in 1962.

After the Muslim conquest of the Maghreb, about 710, Muslim traders moved enslaved people from West, Central and East Africa across the Sahara. They were sold on the coast of the Maghreb, in Egypt and beyond. Estimates are 10 to 18 million people from the 7th to the 20th century.
One route of the trans-Saharan slave trade went from Tripoli through the Fezzan to Bornu. The trade went on until the 20th century, when it was made illegal everywhere.
After the Muslim conquest of the Maghreb, about 710, enslaved people from West, Central and East Africa were sold on the coast of the Maghreb.
Enslaved people who were moved across the Sahara were sold in Egypt. One route went from Egypt in the east to Ghana, Mali and Songhai in the west.
The Kanem-Bornu Empire took part in the trans-Saharan slave trade for centuries. The trade was the base of the wealth of the empire.
In states of the western Sudan, among them Ghana, Mali and Songhai, about a third of the people were slaves.
In the 19th century at least half of the people of the Sokoto Caliphate were slaves.
There was slavery in the Kingdom of Kongo before the Portuguese came.

From the 9th century, traders took Bantu people from the inland of today's Kenya, Mozambique and Tanzania to the coast as slaves. The Indian Ocean slave trade became smaller when slavery was ended in the 19th century.
Omani slave coast of East Africa
Enslaved people of the Indian Ocean slave trade were taken along the Swahili coast and the Horn of Africa. The map data calls this coast, when Oman held it, the Omani Slave Coast.
Southern Arabia: Oman (Indian Ocean slave trade)
The Indian Ocean slave trade took enslaved people, most of them from Africa south of the Sahara, to Southern Arabia and other lands. Muslim slave trading there began in the 7th century.
West coast of India (Indian Ocean slave trade)
The west coast of India was one of the lands of the Indian Ocean slave trade. Muslim slave trading there began in the 7th century.
Java was one of the lands of the Indian Ocean slave trade. Muslim slave trading there began in the 7th century. The trade became smaller when slavery was ended in the 19th century.
Scandinavia in the Viking Age: Norway
In the Viking Age, from about 793, Norse raiders often took the people they met as slaves, called thralls. This ended in Scandinavia in the middle of the 14th century.
Scandinavia in the Viking Age: Denmark
In the Viking Age, from about 793, Norse raiders often took the people they met as slaves, called thralls. This ended in Scandinavia in the middle of the 14th century.
Scandinavia in the Viking Age: Sweden
In the Viking Age, from about 793, Norse raiders often took the people they met as slaves, called thralls. This ended in Scandinavia in the middle of the 14th century.
Before 1066, slavery was common in the British Isles: people became slaves in war, through debt, or by their own choice. Records show slavery in Cornwall in the 9th and 10th centuries.
The people of the Crimean Khanate often raided the lands around them, such as Poland-Lithuania and Muscovy, to take people as slaves.
Slavery was legal in the Ottoman Empire, and it was an important part of its economy and its society.
From the 16th to the 19th centuries, Muslim pirates, most of them from Algiers, raided the coasts and the ships of Europe. They took thousands of people, and sold them or held them as slaves.

In 1452 the pope gave the king of Portugal the right to make certain people who were not Christians slaves for all time. Merchants from Portugal began the slave trade across the Atlantic in the 16th century.

From about 1550 the Portuguese brought enslaved Africans to Brazil to work on sugar farms. Slavery was a main part of the economy of the colony. Brazil got 4 million enslaved people, more than any other country.
Between the 17th and the early 20th centuries, a quarter to a third of the people of some parts of Thailand and Burma were slaves.
Between the 17th and the early 20th centuries, a quarter to a third of the people of some parts of Thailand and Burma were slaves.
In the Joseon period, in times of bad harvests and hunger, many farmers sold themselves into the nobi system, a form of slavery, to stay alive. Korea ended slavery by law in 1894.
Japan banned slavery by law late in the 16th century. But forms of work under a contract and forced work as a punishment went on.
Peter the Great made all house slaves into house serfs in 1723. This in effect made slavery illegal in Russia. Serfdom, a different form of unfree work, ended in 1861.
France banned slavery in Malta when it took the islands in 1798. The National Congress of Malta later confirmed this, though it was in rebellion against the French.
Japan in the Second World War
In its wars in China and the Pacific, the armed forces of Japan used millions of civilians and prisoners of war from many countries as forced workers.

In 1856 and 1857 William Walker made slavery legal again in Nicaragua for a short time. He was defeated and sent out of the country. The map data gives his state the name of his older state in Mexico.
There was slavery in Wallachia until a law ended it in 1856. The source says no more about it.
Russia took Bessarabia in 1812 and kept the slave status of the Roma there. A census of 1858 counted 11,074 Roma slaves in Bessarabia. The source gives no year for the end.
Germany in the Second World War

In the Second World War, Germany ran labour camps. Most of the workers there were Polish and Jewish civilians, taken by force in the occupied countries. By 1944, 20% of all workers were foreigners: civilians or prisoners of war.

The Soviet Union ran forced labour camps, the Gulag. About 14 million prisoners passed through them. From 1954 the state closed the camps step by step. The source gives 1960 as the official end, and marks that date as not checked.
Haiti declared independence and ended slavery.
Slavery was legal in Serbia under the law of the Ottoman Empire. The source says that this held until the end of Ottoman rule in 1804. It names no law of Serbia itself.
Haiti took the Spanish part of the island in 1822 and ended slavery there. The Dominican Republic became independent in 1844 and kept the ban.
Costa Rica was a part of the Federal Republic of Central America, which ended slavery in 1824.
El Salvador was a part of the Federal Republic of Central America, which ended slavery in 1824.
Honduras was a part of the Federal Republic of Central America, which ended slavery in 1824.
Nicaragua was a part of the Federal Republic of Central America, which ended slavery in 1824. In 1856 and 1857 William Walker made slavery legal again for a short time, until he was defeated.
The last slaves in Mexico were freed. The constitution of 1824 had in effect ended slavery.
Greece ended slavery when it became independent.
United Kingdom and most of the British Empire
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force. It ended slavery in most of the British Empire, step by step over six years. It left out the lands of the East India Company and Ceylon.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 40,000 people in South Africa.

The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 also held for the British colonies in Australia. But later, 55,000 to 62,500 South Sea Islanders were taken to Australia for work, many by force or by tricks. Some Indigenous people had forced labour until the late 1970s. A newer law is the Modern Slavery Act 2018.

Upper Canada passed the Act Against Slavery in 1793. Courts and local laws ended most slavery by the colonists early in the 1800s. Slavery stayed legal until the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force in 1834. Some First Nations had slavery until the later 1800s.

Ireland was a part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland when the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force in 1834. Long before, in 1171, the Council of Armagh freed all English slaves in Ireland.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 20,000 people in Mauritius. The source gives the year of the law, not the day on which it started in Mauritius.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force in 1834. The freed people then had to work on as "apprentices". Barbados was the first colony to end that, on 1 August 1838.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force in 1834. The freed people then had to work on as "apprentices". In 1838 the apprentices of Trinidad held angry meetings against two more years of it.
Antigua gave full freedom on the day that the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force. It did not use the years as "apprentices" that the law let the other colonies use.
The Bahamas was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
British Honduras was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
Dominica was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
Grenada was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
British Guiana was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
Saint Lucia was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
Saint Vincent was a British colony in the West Indies. The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 by law freed 700,000 people in the West Indies from 1834. The source does not name each colony.
Britain banned the trade in slaves when it took the islands in 1815, and ended slavery in 1835. The freed people had to work on for their former owners for six more years.

In Māori society, prisoners of war became slaves. The Treaty of Waitangi outlawed slavery in 1840. But slavery did not end completely until the government had control of the whole country, after the wars of the mid-1860s.
Spain ended slavery, but not in its colonies. Cuba and Puerto Rico have entries of their own.
India (lands of the East India Company)
The Indian Slavery Act of 1843 ended slavery in the lands that the East India Company held.
Bengal (lands of the East India Company)
The Indian Slavery Act of 1843 ended slavery in the lands that the East India Company held. Bengal was one of them: its government had made rules against the trade in slaves in 1774.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 left out the island of Ceylon. The source says that this exception was ended in 1843.
Tunisia ended slavery under the rule of Ahmed Bey.
France ended slavery in its colonies. It had ended slavery in all its lands in 1794, and Napoleon brought it back in 1802 in the colonies that grew sugar cane.
France ended slavery in its colonies in 1848. In that year Gabon was founded as a settlement for freed slaves.
France formally banned slavery in Algeria in 1848. But the French there were slow to free the slaves, for fear of unrest. Slavery and the trade in slaves went on into the early 20th century.
Denmark ended slavery in its colony, the Danish West Indies, in 1848, after a revolt of the slaves there. Denmark had banned its trade in slaves across the Atlantic from 1803.
Panama was a part of New Granada, which ended slavery in 1851.
Argentina ended slavery with its new federal constitution.
Moldavia ended slavery in 1855 and Wallachia in 1856. The two are lands of Romania today.
Russia banned the Kazakhs from having slaves in 1859. Slavery went on in some areas to the end of the century. The source page marks this line: it needs a better source.
The Indian Penal Code of 1861 banned slavery in the lands of India under British rule. The source does not name the lands. The map data draws this land as British from 1849.
The Netherlands ended slavery in its colonies.
The Netherlands ended slavery in its colonies. 33,000 people were freed in Suriname.
The Netherlands ended slavery in its colonies in 1863. The source says that the number of people freed in the East Indies is not known.
The Netherlands ended slavery in its colonies in 1863. This freed 12,000 people in Curaçao and its dependencies.
The Thirteenth Amendment ended slavery, except as punishment for a crime. Some states had ended slavery before.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. Angola was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. Mozambique was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. Cape Verde was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. Portuguese Guinea was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. São Tomé and Príncipe was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
Portugal ended slavery in all its lands and colonies in 1869. Portuguese Timor was a Portuguese colony then. The source does not name each colony.
The British colony Gold Coast ended slavery in 1874. In 1998 Ghana banned the forced service of girls in shrines. The map data draws this land as British from 1898.

Slavery was legal in Cyprus under the law of the Ottoman Empire until 1878. In that year Cyprus came under British rule, and slavery had no standing in British law. The source names no law for Cyprus itself.
Bulgaria ended slavery when it became independent. Its constitution says that a slave who enters Bulgaria is free at once.
Korea ended slavery by law. In practice it went on until 1930.
Korea ended slavery by law in 1894. In practice it went on until 1930. Korea was one country then.
Japan took Taiwan in 1895. The source says that slavery was ended in Japan by then.
Laos became a French colony in 1893. France ended slavery in Laos in 1898, but slavery went on in many parts of Laos until the 1920s.
France ended slavery on the island of Anjouan (Ndzuwani). The source says nothing of the other islands of the Comoros.
German Cameroon started to end slavery step by step in 1902. The source gives no year for the end of that.
Slavery ended in British East Africa.
Slavery was formally ended in French West Africa. In practice it went on for decades.

Senegal was a part of French West Africa. Slavery was formally ended there in 1905. Up to one million people became free, but in practice slavery went on for decades. The source does not name each colony.

Guinea was a part of French West Africa. Slavery was formally ended there in 1905. Up to one million people became free, but in practice slavery went on for decades. The source does not name each colony.

Ivory Coast was a part of French West Africa. Slavery was formally ended there in 1905. Up to one million people became free, but in practice slavery went on for decades. The source does not name each colony.

The land of Burkina Faso was a part of French West Africa. Slavery was formally ended there in 1905. Up to one million people became free, but in practice slavery went on for decades. The source does not name each colony.

Dahomey was a part of French West Africa. Slavery was formally ended there in 1905. Up to one million people became free, but in practice slavery went on for decades. The source does not name each colony.
Slavery ended in Barotseland, in the west of the Zambia of today.

Italy ended slavery in Italian Somaliland with a series of decrees from 1897 to 1907. They banned the trade in slaves and ended "domestic servitude" step by step. The first Italian tries had mostly failed.
Belgium took over the Congo Free State in 1908. The source says that this ended the practice of slavery there.
A law of 1906 ended slavery in China from 31 January 1910.

Slavery was legal in Albania under the law of the Ottoman Empire. The source says that this held until the end of Ottoman rule and the start of the Principality of Albania in 1914. It names no law of Albania itself.
There was open slavery in Palestine into the 20th century. The British Mandate of Palestine started in 1920. It ended slavery as an institution, because British law did not recognise slavery.
There was open slavery in Palestine into the 20th century. The British Mandate of Palestine started in 1920. It ended slavery as an institution, because British law did not recognise slavery.
The Emirate of Afghanistan ended slavery.
Slavery ended in the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan.
South Sudan was a part of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, where slavery ended in 1924.
The slavery that local African rulers practised in Sierra Leone was ended.
Slavery was legal in the Sultanate of Brunei until the 20th century. Brunei was a British protectorate from 1888. A law formally ended slavery in 1928.
Persia ended slavery and made it a crime.
The British ended slavery by law in the Emirate of Transjordan in 1929. There were still reports of slavery in practice in the 1940s.
The French authorities formally ended slavery in Lebanon in 1931. In that year France ratified the Slavery Convention of 1926 for Syria and Lebanon.
The French authorities formally ended slavery in Syria in 1931. In that year France ratified the Slavery Convention of 1926 for Syria and Lebanon.

Italy made two laws against slavery in 1935 and 1936, when it held Ethiopia. The source says that they freed 420,000 people. Then Emperor Haile Selassie came back, and ended slavery by law on 26 August 1942.
Niger ended slavery. It became a crime there in 2003.
The constitution of Morocco ended slavery. Slavery in homes went on.
The source says that slavery was ended in 1979, when the dictator Francisco Macías Nguema was overthrown. It does not say more. The map data has this land with no overlap from 1973.
Mauritania ended slavery by law, the last country to do so. The ban was not enforced, and many people were still held as slaves. Slavery became a crime there in 2007.
